subject: biochemistry
title: Biochemistry mixed rapid review: high-yield essentials

steps.tx: Biochemistry mixed review covers several high-yield facts. **Galactosaemia** from uridyl transferase deficiency causes convulsions, cataract and mental retardation, and is autosomal recessive. **Sickle cell anaemia** results from a **missense** mutation changing glutamate to valine at position 6 of the beta globin chain. Thiamine deficiency causes Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.
steps.say: Biochemistry mixed review covers several high-yield facts. Galactosaemia, from uridyl transferase deficiency, causes convulsions, cataract and mental retardation, and is autosomal recessive. Sickle cell anaemia results from a missense mutation changing glutamate to valine at position 6 of the beta globin chain. Thiamine deficiency causes Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.

steps.tx: Hormones and second messengers are frequently tested. **Gs** and **Gq** are stimulatory G proteins whereas **Gi** is inhibitory. Insulin acts through **tyrosine kinase** receptors, which are enzymatic receptors. **Cyclic GMP** is a second messenger, while calcium and cAMP are also second messengers; the odd one out in the MCQ was none.
steps.say: Hormones and second messengers are frequently tested. Gs and Gq are stimulatory G proteins, whereas Gi is inhibitory. Insulin acts through tyrosine kinase receptors, which are enzymatic receptors. Cyclic GMP is a second messenger, as are cyclic AMP and calcium.

steps.tx: Vitamins and nutrition are high yield. **Vitamin D** acts as a hormone via intranuclear receptors, and **1,25 dihydroxy cholecalciferol** is its most potent, metabolically active form. Energy yield is 4 kcal per gram for carbohydrates and proteins, and 9 kcal per gram for fats. Pyridoxine requirement tracks protein intake.
steps.say: Vitamins and nutrition are high yield. Vitamin D acts as a hormone through intranuclear receptors, and one, twenty five dihydroxy cholecalciferol, is the most potent active form. Carbohydrates and proteins yield 4 kilocalories per gram, while fats yield 9 kilocalories per gram. Pyridoxine requirement tracks protein intake.

steps.tx: Blood group genetics is often examined. The **ABO** system lies on the long arm of **chromosome 9** and has three alleles, A, B and O. ABO is an example of **codominance**, where both alleles contribute to the phenotype. **HLA** genes lie on the short arm of chromosome 6.
steps.say: Blood group genetics is often examined. The ABO system lies on the long arm of chromosome nine and has three alleles, A, B and O. ABO is an example of codominance, where both alleles contribute to the phenotype. HLA genes lie on the short arm of chromosome six.

steps.tx: Porphyrias and haemoglobin switching are tested. **Acute intermittent porphyria** is autosomal dominant and results from deficiency of **porphobilinogen deaminase**, causing colicky abdominal pain and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Haemoglobin switches from fetal to adult synthesis around **36 weeks** of gestation, when beta chain synthesis exceeds gamma chain synthesis.

steps.tx: Digestion and physiology complete the review. **Enteropeptidase**, formerly enterokinase, activates trypsinogen, so its deficiency mainly reduces protein-digesting enzymes. Positive nitrogen balance occurs in growing children and pregnancy, while negative balance follows starvation and trauma. Remember that the **Feulgen reaction** stains DNA red.
